International Protection Bill 2026 
The International Protection Bill 2026, published in January 2026, represents a significant reform of 
Ireland’s international protection system and will apply to all new applications made from 12 June 2026 
onwards, with transitional arrangements in place for applications submitted prior to that date. The Bill 
introduces legally binding timelines for application processing, appeals and return decisions.  As of 23 
January 2026, there are approximately 1,000 international protection applicants accommodated 
across IPAS centres in County Tipperary, comprising a mix of individuals and families across both North 
and South of the county. The proposed legislative changes are expected to reduce the length of time 
applicants spend within the protection system, which may have implications for accommodation 
turnover, demand for local services and medium-term integration planning at county level.

Reach Enterprise HUB, Roscrea

spaces for community benefit. The project, funded through the Rural Regeneration & Development 
Fund, transformed a former Tesco store into a modern innovation hub. The facility provides office 
spaces for local entrepreneurs, community meeting rooms, and training facilities. The Hub acts as a focal

Tipperary County Council is proud to support Ireland’s first Circular Cups for Community Events 
initiative, developed by the Southern Region Waste Planning Office in partnership with Local 
Authorities across the Southern Waste Region* and IRD Duhallow. This pioneering programme 
provides local not-for-profit community events with access to high-quality reusable cups, designed 
to eliminate single-use waste at their events. 
How It Works: 
• Cups are delivered clean to event locations. 
• After the event, they are collected and professionally washed at a dedicated facility. 
• Each cup can be reused up to 300 times, creating a truly circular solution. 
• Organisers pay only for transportation and a nominal washing fee, plus a deposit for 
losses. 
 
The booking system is now live https://reusablecups.tenvito.com, and cups will be available for 
eligible events starting January 12th, 2026. (*Southern Waste Region including local authorities in counties 
Tipperary, Limerick, Clare, Cork, Waterford, Kerry, Wexford, Kilkenny and Carlow).

Families in Tipperary preparing to welcome a new baby can now apply for a free cloth nappy 
starter kit through the Cloth Nappy Incentive Scheme, a sustainability initiative led by VOICE

The scheme offers free Cloth Nappy Starter Kits to antenatal patients at TUH. Each kit 
includes: 
• 
10 high-quality reusable cloth nappies 
• 
12 reusable cloth wipes 
• 
Waterproof storage bag for used nappies 
•

• 
Comprehensive guidance on use and care 
 
This year, the Cloth Nappy Library has joined the initiative, providing workshops and one-on-one 
support to help parents understand different types of cloth nappies, how to use and wash them, 
and offering ongoing guidance. This initiative comes in response to the growing environmental 
impact of disposable nappies. Currently Ireland sends an estimated one million disposable nappies 
to landfill every day. According to the EPA Household Waste Characterisation Report (2022), 
nappies account for 10% of kerbside residual waste, totalling over 75,000 tonnes annually, making 
them the third largest fraction of household waste. Reusable cloth nappies offer a sustainable 
alternative with a 25% lower carbon footprint across their lifecycle compared to disposables as
